To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in patients with myocardium infarction, the degree of systolic blood response to dobutamin stress is determined by left ventricular function (as expressed by wall motion score index) and by baseline systolic blood pressures.

systolic blood pressure increase > or =30 mm Hg and decrease > or = 15 mm Hg are predictors of more severe functional impairment in patients with prior myocardium infarction undergoing dobutamine stress echocardiography.

in patients with myocardical infarction, systolic blood pressure and heart rate increase from rest to peak stress, and that systolic blood pressure drop > or =20 mm Hg is a marker of more severely impaired left ventricular function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between systolic blood pressure changes and the severity of myocardial ischemic abnormalities during dobutamine stress echocardiography.
the functional significance of dobutamine-induced SBP response.
the study of the predictors of SBP changes during dobutamine stress in patients with previous acute myocardial infarcts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dobutamine-induced hypotensive response in patients with prior myocardium infarction is associated with more severe functional abnormalities.

the systolic blood pressure drop during dobutamine stress echocardiography is a marker of more extensive and severe left ventricular dysfunction in patients with myocardium infarction, whereas systolic blood pressure increase is more likely to occur in patients with less severe left ventricular impairment.

a decrease of SBP during dobutamine stress echocardiography may be a marker of a more severe functional impairment, but a rise of SBP may be due to a variety of reasons, including the presence of hypertension and/or the use of calcium channel blockers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in patients with myocardium infarction systolic blood pressure is a good marker of left ventricular function.
in patients with myocardical infarction, dobutamine induced hypotension is associated with more severe left ventricular functional abnormalities.
dobutamine stress echocardiography is a safe, well-tolerated, and reliable test for the assessment of patients with myocardial ischemia.

the SBP response is a powerful predictor of left ventricular function in patients with previous acute myocardial infarct.
the systolic blood pressure is a marker of the severity of the underlying disease.
